'''Gregory Maxwell "Max" Kelly''' (5 June 1930 – 26 January 2007) was an Australian mathematician who worked on [[category theory]].

==Biography==
Kelly was born in [[Bondi, New South Wales]], [[Australia]], on 5 June 1930.<ref name="mactutor">{{MacTutor Biography|id=Kelly_Max}}</ref>  He obtained his [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] at [[Cambridge University]] in [[homological algebra]] in 1957, publishing his first paper in that area in 1959, ''Single-space axioms for homology theory''.<ref name="mactutor"/><ref name="mgp">{{MathGenealogy|name=Gregory Maxwell (Max) Kelly}}</ref>  He taught in the Pure Mathematics department at the [[University of Sydney]] from 1957 to 1966, rising from lecturer to reader.<ref name="mactutor"/>  During 1963–1965 he was a visiting fellow at [[Tulane University]] and the [[University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign|University of Illinois]],<ref name="mactutor"/> where with [[Samuel Eilenberg]] he formalized and developed the notion of an [[enriched category]] based on intuitions then in the air about making the [[hom set|homsets]] of a [[category (mathematics)|category]] just as abstract as the objects themselves.{{citation needed|date=December 2020}}

He subsequently developed the notion in considerably more detail in his 1982 monograph ''Basic Concepts of Enriched Category Theory''.<ref>{{cite book|last=Kelly|first=Gregory Maxwell|title=Basic Concepts of Enriched Category Theory|url=http://tac.mta.ca/tac/reprints/articles/10/tr10abs.html|year=1982|publisher=[[Cambridge University Press]]|isbn=978-0-521-28702-9}}</ref>  Let <math>\cal V</math> be a [[monoidal category]], and denote by {{nowrap|<math>\cal V</math>-Cat}} the category of {{nowrap|<math>\cal V</math>-enriched}} categories.  Among other things, Kelly showed that {{nowrap|<math>\cal V</math>-Cat}} has all weighted limits and colimits even when <math>\cal V</math> does not have all ordinary [[limits and colimits]].  He also developed the enriched counterparts of [[Kan extension]]s, density of the [[Yoneda embedding]], and essentially algebraic theories.{{citation needed|date=December 2020}}

In 1967 Kelly was appointed Professor of Pure Mathematics at the [[University of New South Wales]].<ref name="mactutor"/> In 1972 he was elected a [[Fellow of the Australian Academy of Science]].{{citation needed|date=December 2020}} He returned to the University of Sydney in 1973, serving as Professor of Mathematics until his retirement in 1992.<ref name="mactutor"/>  In 2001 he was awarded the Australian government's [[Centenary Medal]].  He continued to participate{{dubious|date=December 2020}} in the department as professorial fellow and professor emeritus until his death at age 76 on 26 January 2007.<ref name="mactutor"/>

Kelly worked on many other aspects of category theory besides enriched categories, both individually and in a number of collaborations.{{citation needed|date=December 2020}} His PhD students include [[Ross Street]].<ref name="mgp" />
